paper.title_en: ProducingμBq/m$^{3}$-level low-$^{226}$Ra ultrapure water for the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory
paper.abstract_en: The Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO), a 20 kton low-background liquid-scintillator (LS) detector, was designed primarily to determine the neutrino mass ordering. JUNO requires ultrapure water (UPW) with a $^{226}$Ra concentration < 50 $\upmu$Bq/m$^3$ because of the direct liquid-liquid contact between LS and UPW during detector filling. To meet this stringent requirement, a high-sensitivity measurement system capable of detecting $^{226}$Ra in water down to 3.9 $\upmu$Bq/m$^3$ was developed, and the 100 t/h UPW production process was optimized. By integrating selective ion-exchange resin with membrane-based separation technologies, the system consistently produced UPW with a $^{226}$Ra concentration of < 4 $\upmu$Bq/m$^3$, exceeding the JUNO specification and, to our knowledge, representing one of the lowest reported levels achieved at this engineering scale. This paper describes the design and implementation of JUNO's UPW system and the high-sensitivity $^{226}$Ra measurement platform, together with a systematic evaluation of $^{226}$Ra removal efficiencies across the purification train and validation of the final water quality.
